extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism ontology record from primary anti-QS assays, RT-qPCR, biofilm/swarming assays, and docking text. Mechanism claims are bounded; docking is not treated as biochemical binding proof.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: cyclo(L-Tyr-L-Pro) shows direct anti-quorum-sensing phenotypes in C. violaceum CV026 and P. aeruginosa PA01, including reduced violacein, pyocyanin, protease, elastase, swarming, biofilm, and QS gene expression at sub-MIC concentration.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=5:Anti-QS Activity; xml:sec=6:Inhibitory Effects on Biofilm Formation; xml:sec=7:QS Gene Expression

mechanism_claims.limitations: Phenotypic and expression assays support QS pathway modulation but do not by themselves prove direct receptor binding.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Molecular docking supports a competitive-binding model for CviR and LasR receptor pockets, with reported binding energies and hydrogen-bond contacts for cyclo(L-Tyr-L-Pro).
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: cyclo(L-Tyr-L-Pro) with CviR and LasR models
mechanism_claims.limitations: Docking is computational support only; no SPR/ITC/crystallographic binding assay for the compound-receptor complex is present in local material.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: At 0.5 mg/mL the compound is below one-tenth MIC and the paper frames the observed effects as anti-virulence/QS inhibition rather than direct bacterial killing.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: cyclo(L-Tyr-L-Pro) at 0.5 mg/mL in P. aeruginosa PA01 assays
mechanism_claims.limitations: This boundary does not exclude antimicrobial activity at MIC concentrations; it prevents overclaiming sub-MIC QS assays as bactericidal toxicity.

source_review_notes: Generic framework mechanism placeholders were replaced with source-specific anti-QS/docking claims.
No unsupported protein-synthesis or nucleic-acid-binding mechanism is retained.
Computational docking remains a caution, not direct biochemical proof.
